title: openpractice-patient-gateway 1.0
description: Canonical message schema for the patient gateway contract between HealthLinc (the owner's working name for the ecosystem patient app) and openPractice. Owned by opensoft/openPractice-spec change define-patient-gateway-and-escalation; to be referenced by digest from the required HealthLinc companion change. Every object is closed (additionalProperties false). Reasons are codes. References are opaque or (issuer, namespace, value) triples. message_id is a random UUID and is the idempotency key; no key carries PHI. The only free-text fields are the administrative inquiry body, the administrative reply body, and the patient-proposed demographic and coverage values; a clinical inquiry carries no body. The entitlement result always grants urgent_escalation, billing_contact and own_records_access; a payment hold may withhold only clinical_messaging_nonurgent, scheduling_new_nonurgent and medical_ai_consult, and is never revealed to a representative without billing scope. An inquiry names where its conversation lives: healthlinc (HealthLinc's coach) or medxfactory (medXfactory's medical AI). Patient notices carry no amount or reason text. A deployment whose operator agreement is not verified is refused with operator_agreement_unverified. 1.0 carries no appointment or payment operations; they come as later MINOR versions. A receiver accepts any 1.x message and rejects any other MAJOR with reason unsupported_major_version.

issuer.description: A deployment's configured, stable issuer identifier, unique across deployments and never derived from a host path (EB-02).

actorRef.description: Opaque reference to a Roster entry (a person, a remote VA or a named agent, AM-01, AM-04) or an integration identity. Never a name.

opaqueRef.description: Opaque reference. Carries no name, date of birth, contact detail, amount or clinical content.

urgency.description: Applied or proposed urgency. Ordered routine < priority < urgent. openPractice never lowers an applied urgency (ER-03).

capability.description: Coded gateway capability. urgent_escalation, billing_contact and own_records_access are always granted to a linked patient (PG-03). Non-urgent means applied urgency routine only (ruling 41). medical_ai_consult covers non-urgent consults with medXfactory's medical AI (ruling 52). HealthLinc's coach is HealthLinc's own, has no capability, and is never gated by the practice.

withholdableCapability.description: Capabilities that may be withheld. The three always-granted capabilities are not in this list, so they can never be withheld.

withholdReason.description: Coded reason a capability is withheld. No amount, balance or clinical detail is ever given.

adminTopic.description: HealthLinc's proposed administrative topic, used by openPractice's fixed rules to pick a lane.

healthlincRef.description: A HealthLinc account or message reference: (HealthLinc issuer, healthlinc, value). The namespace token healthlinc is a design call (design.md DC-1).

openpracticeRef.description: An openPractice patient reference: (openPractice issuer, openpractice, value), as EB-01.

conversationSource.description: Where the patient's conversation lives (ruling 51): healthlinc for a conversation HealthLinc holds (a coach conversation, a direct message to the doctor, or an administrative thread), medxfactory for a conversation with medXfactory's medical AI. openPractice stores no clinical content from either.

proposalSource.description: Who proposed the category and urgency: coach_triage (HealthLinc's coach), medical_ai_triage (medXfactory's medical AI) or patient_checklist (HealthLinc's red-flag checklist for a message written straight to the doctor with no AI triage; ruling 71).

conversationRef.description: Reference to the conversation in the system that holds it: (issuer, healthlinc or medxfactory, value). Its namespace matches conversation_source. The namespace token medxfactory is a design call (design.md DC-37).

answerTypeRef.description: A practice-approved read-only answer type and its version (change define-actors-agents-and-work-inbox AH-05 exception 1).

codedText.description: Patient-reported coded value with optional patient-entered text, as in the EB-06 snapshot.

legalName.description: Structured legal name, the same shape as the openpractice-ehr-patient-link snapshot. A single-name person carries only that name.

confidentialCommunication.description: PR-05 confidential-communication instructions, proposed by the patient.

hold_policy_ref.description: The approved payment-hold policy version that applied (PH-03).

entitlementRequest.description: HealthLinc asks which capabilities a linked patient holds now (PG-03).

message_id.description: Random UUID. It is the idempotency key: every retry reuses it. It never carries PHI.

gateway_link_id.description: Minted by openPractice in link.result; names one HealthLinc-to-openPractice link for its whole life (PG-05).

entitlementResult.description: openPractice answers with coded capabilities and coded reasons only (PG-03, PG-04, PG-06).

message_id.description: Random UUID. It is the idempotency key: every retry reuses it. It never carries PHI.

gateway_link_id.description: Minted by openPractice in link.result; names one HealthLinc-to-openPractice link for its whole life (PG-05).

link_kind.description: Whether the link is the patient's own or a representative's (PG-05, PG-06).

representative_billing_scope.description: For a representative link: whether the proxy policy lets this representative see the patient's billing. When false, a payment hold is never revealed: withheld capabilities carry representative_scope, and no hold-policy reference is sent (PG-06).

valid_until.description: HealthLinc re-asks after this time. A stale result never removes an always-granted capability.

capabilities.description: Granted capabilities. Always includes urgent_escalation, billing_contact and own_records_access for a linked patient, whatever the registry, membership or hold status (PG-03, PH-02).

capability.description: A payment hold may withhold only these three capabilities (PH-01).

linkRequest.description: HealthLinc asks openPractice to link a HealthLinc account to an openPractice patient (PG-05, PG-06). openPractice mints gateway_link_id in link.result.

message_id.description: Random UUID. It is the idempotency key: every retry reuses it. It never carries PHI.

healthlinc_account.description: The HealthLinc account asking for the link: the patient's own account, or the representative's.

method.description: Coded identity-verification method of the account holder. The closed list is decided in planning. Possession of a device, a telephone number or an invitation code is never by itself verified identity.

identity_claim.description: Identifies the patient whose openPractice record is to be linked: a practice-issued invitation reference, or the legal name and date of birth, which staff compare by exact match (PR-08). No link is ever made from matching alone.

representative.description: Present only for a representative link (PG-06).

authority_ref.description: Reference to the documented authority, held by the practice or HealthLinc.

linkResult.description: openPractice reports the link outcome. A link becomes linked only after a named human confirms the verified identity (PG-05).

message_id.description: Random UUID. It is the idempotency key: every retry reuses it. It never carries PHI.

linkRevoked.description: Either side revokes a gateway link. Revocation wins over any concurrent confirmation (PG-07).

proposalSubmitted.description: A patient-submitted change. It enters openPractice as a proposal with patient provenance and is never applied automatically (PG-08, PG-09).

coverage.description: A proposed PR-07 coverage change. 1.0 carries no attachments such as card images (design.md DC-20).

coverage_ref.description: Opaque reference to the registry coverage being updated or ended.

inquirySubmitted.description: HealthLinc submits a patient question or an escalation to the patient's human doctor, from a conversation HealthLinc holds (a coach conversation, a direct message to the doctor or an administrative thread) or a medXfactory medical-AI conversation (rulings 51 and 71). A clinical question carries no body: no clinical content enters openPractice (ER-01, ER-05).

inquiry_ref.description: HealthLinc's reference for the patient's request. HealthLinc stays the store of the request.

reply_path_ref.description: Opaque reference to the HealthLinc conversation a reply goes into.

proposed_category.description: Proposed by the source named in proposal_source (rulings 44, 51 and 71). An uncertain category is proposed as clinical, and a message written straight to the doctor is clinical.

proposed_urgency.description: From an AI, proposed with the conservative default: an uncertain urgency is proposed as urgent (ruling 51). From patient_checklist: urgent on any red flag, routine with none, priority when the checklist is skipped, and never lower than the patient chose (ruling 71). openPractice never lowers it (ER-03).

triage_ref.description: Opaque reference to the proposing triage output: the coach's or medical AI's triage and model version, or the patient's checklist response; the system that holds the conversation keeps the detail.

human_requested.description: True when the patient asked for a person, or said an answer did not answer the question. openPractice routes the item to staff and never to a read-only answer (ER-10).

body.description: Administrative question text. Present only when proposed_category is administrative. It may contain PHI, is stored under Principle I safeguards, and is never logged (PG-10, PG-13).

split.description: Present when HealthLinc split a mixed question into parts (ER-12).

recategorizes_routing_id.description: Set when HealthLinc resubmits after inquiry.recategorized.

inquiryAck.description: openPractice accepts and routes an inquiry, or rejects it with a coded reason. An urgent inquiry is never rejected for a withheld capability (ER-09).
